What is ODF? Apply Now What is ODF? ODF helps more people start the best companies. Great fit You have a track record of shipping impressive things. You’re 100 % committed (or soon committing) to starting a company. You gain energy from helping other founders win. Not a fit You’ve already raised beyond pre-seed / found product-market fit. You’re building something that can’t reach venture scale. Your main customer base will remain outside the US. You already have a team. What You Get One-week onboarding in SF with 80-100 high-momentum builders. Lifetime access to our 3000+-member community & events. >$800 k in perks (AWS, Stripe, Mercury, Carta, etc.). Library of workshops and how-tos on fundraising, product, hiring. Time, Place & Cost Presence: You must attend the full SF sprint (five business days). Ongoing: How much time you invest in ODF for the rest of the year is up to you. You’ll continue to have access to a lively online community and IRL events. Contribution: We’re a non-dilutive program with a Pay-what-you-can model; we suggest $1000 USD which covers venue, food, and year-round community infrastructure. Outcomes & Alumni Wins ODF alumni have collectively raised >$2 B and include breakout companies like Levels, Settle, Finch, Loyal, and Grow Therapy . "Meeting (my co-founder) Akshay was literally a gift from god." — Mike Shebat, Traba CEO (ODF6) Admissions Snapshot

Starting Companies | The Deep End Start a company THE DEEP END PROBLEMS WORTH SOLVING The Meta-Problem of Starting Companies Technology is the best mechanism we have to solve complex, societal challenges. The most optimal way to solve them is not to tackle a specific one but rather focus on the meta problem of helping more people start more challenge-solving companies. We talk to founders and investors on the frontiers of the problem to help you understand what’s going on. Click to play Watch full episode Table of Contents Table of Contents 01. The Problem 02. Problem Worth Solving 03. Bottlenecks Access to Capital Access to Capital — Regulation — Regulation — Cultural Defaults — Cultural Defaults — Technical Barriers — Technical Barriers — Infrastructure — Infrastructure — Community — Community — Legibility of Problems — Legibility of Problems The Problem At On Deck, we believe technology is the best mechanism we have to solve complex societal problems. Climate, affordable housing, access to food, the rise of AI, education and low-cost transportation are all issues that startups are best suited to bring their technological solutions to the mass market. Startups are lean, fast-growing, and well-governed. The newness of startups means that communication costs are low and they get to avoid a lot of the bureaucracy that comes with larger more established companies or governments.
